scope: Reproduced and investigated gaps; the source-hashed line inventory is separate. Closed means the cited bounded regression is covered, not exhaustive format support.

status_definitions.closed: Reproduced gap fixed and protected by named evidence.
status_definitions.partial: Named evidence covers a bounded subset; the stated remainder remains open.
status_definitions.guarded: Unsupported operation is rejected explicitly before writing output.
status_definitions.open: Known unsupported behavior or missing acceptance coverage.
status_definitions.in_progress: Active work; not yet represented as a passing fix.

gaps.finding: Dense notes reserve space and continue without overlapping body content.
Notes retain ordered rich paragraphs, tables, owned pictures and hyperlinks.
Document defaults, basedOn inheritance, character/table styles and explicit defaults are retained.
Document-local IDs and level overrides preserve independent list sequences and repeated saves.
Independent openpyxl/python-pptx fixtures exercise styles, charts, pivots, template parts, notes and media ownership.

Open XML SDK and LibreOffice/Poppler gates validate schema and repeated-save rendering, retain exact-byte schema receipts and actual page PNGs, and report qualified native-only renderer limitations separately from visual passes.

Twenty-three reviewed page images cover notes, note continuation, first/even/default stories, columns, tall tables, structural create/edit/remove workflows, three native frame wrap modes and rich nested cells on pinned Linux Flutter 3.44.0. Other platforms and arbitrary scripts/fonts remain unproven.
The source-hashed coverage inventory lists every unhit instrumented line and absent file. Formula/PDF/report branches and many Office combinations remain unproven.

Strict five-command CLI exposes 67 operations; every operation has a committed scenario. Independently authored expectations cover multi-format edits plus creation, modification and removal of Word tables, TOCs, bookmark references, threaded comments, picture wrapping and positioned frames.
All six header/footer variants and notes retain owned image data; replacement/reorder does not overwrite shared payloads.
Imports and writes follow main/styles/notes/settings relationships instead of assuming fixed package filenames.
Drawing links, chart transforms, pivot cache attributes and font-property ordering produce schema-valid output.
Pixel-to-column conversion follows the maximum-digit-width formula; untouched source precision and hidden/grouped/widthless column properties survive edits.
Rich text, scalar font/color edits, hard breaks, paragraphs, templates, transitions, chart transforms and axis IDs survive import/save.
A supported Choice or Fallback is selected once in all modeled Word stories.
Page numbering, grids, borders, custom columns, gutter, line-number settings and section history survive unrelated edits and cloning.
Referenced built-ins absent from an imported style catalog are written with their known parent styles.
LF/CRLF/CR serialize as real Word breaks, tabs survive, and typed page/column breaks remain distinct.
Replacing the viewport triggers layout before painting so its extent is initialized and later pages are visible.
A document revision captured before asynchronous save prevents later edits from being marked clean or closed by an earlier upload.
Preview follows owning parts for notes and workbook order/names, preserves tabs/breaks and explicit false formatting, including package-root main parts.
An independently authored exact output manifest is cleaned narrowly before producers and verified after generation; corruption controls reject absent groups and unexpected files.

Imported altChunk block references, original payload identity, content types and owning-part relationships survive edits, moves and repeated exports. This is preservation; Quds does not render the embedded content.

Live block controls and paired inline boundaries preserve native wrapper attributes, IDs, aliases, tags, sdtPr and sdtEndPr through supported edits and three direct/isolate cycles. Nested body, note, table and frame controls use their real mutable parents. Single-paragraph block controls, including nested shells, are also retained in all six header/footer variants and comments. The original unchanged loss probe passes.
gaps.limits: UI lock/data-binding behavior, repeating-section semantics and arbitrary topology remain open. Inline controls containing drawings/equations, multi-paragraph or non-paragraph controls in paragraph-only auxiliary stories, row/cell wrappers, boundary-crossing edits and duplicate-ID insertion fail explicitly before mutation. Native comment controls require separate renderer limitation reporting; see FID-065.

gaps.finding: Typed zero-width native endpoints preserve exact IDs, names, attributes, overlap order, empty ranges and partial/cross-paragraph ranges through edits, cloning, history and three exports. REF caches use exact marked UTF-16 text and isolate textbox stories. The original unchanged loss probe now passes.
gaps.limits: Mixed text-and-drawing anchor endpoint order remains outside the block drawing model. Duplicate-producing copies and deletion of only one cross-paragraph endpoint are guarded until safe remapping is implemented. Arbitrary rich complex-field refresh remains FID-049.

gaps.finding: Native comment replies and resolved state join through final comment paragraph IDs independently of numeric comment IDs, including reverse source order and mixed-case hexadecimal IDs. Three cycles retain the anchors and source rendering.
The script refuses a sheet rename if formulas, names, charts or pivots refer to it; full reference rewriting is not implemented.
The script refuses slide reorder when presentation sections would also need rewriting.
Column conversion defaults to maximum-digit-width7 and accepts an explicit metric in helpers; normal-style font measurement is not automatic.
LibreOffice repeated-cycle stability is verified; Microsoft Office visual equivalence and interactive native UI behavior are not certified.

Imported documents without a style catalog retain sparse paragraph and run properties. Saving no longer invents global fonts or paragraph after-spacing that changes rendering; explicit edits still export.

gaps.area: Note source whitespace and marker formatting
gaps.finding: Imported note separator whitespace, including no space, spaces and tabs, survives exactly. Note-mark run properties retain their original XML or absence. XML space inheritance is respected. Newly created notes retain a conventional superscript marker and one separator.
gaps.limits: The original leading-marker regression is extended by FID-040 to arbitrary positions, marker absence, later paragraphs and nested cells. Whole-note text replacement intentionally replaces rich content.

gaps.finding: Cloning a section reserves existing revision-history IDs and allocates a distinct stable ID without changing the historical section payload. Original and cloned host exports validate independently.

gaps.area: Imported table border absence and inheritance
gaps.finding: Source table properties retain absent, inherited and explicit nil borders distinctly. Disabling inherited borders writes an explicit override; new tables keep their existing defaults.
gaps.limits: Untouched unmodeled per-edge source XML is retained, but the editable model has one border/color/width tuple. A deliberate border edit emits six uniform edges; independent per-edge editing is not implemented.

gaps.area: Picture wrap distance and omitted attributes
gaps.finding: Picture wrap distances retain zero and sub-eight-point values. Imported omitted attributes remain absent, while explicit zero and later explicit assignments remain observable; visual copies preserve the baseline and edit intent.

gaps.area: Split identity and style namespace editing
gaps.finding: Splitting a paragraph does not duplicate its bookmark identity or restart marker; undo/redo remains stable. Style edits bind generated XML properties to the Word namespace even when an imported w prefix refers to another namespace.

gaps.area: Intermediate list clear and empty format range
gaps.finding: Clearing inherited or direct list numbering exports an explicit suppression override that survives style refresh, clone/history and three save/reopen cycles. Reapplying a list or numbered style restores numbering. Empty script formatting ranges fail with an indexed step diagnostic before replacing output.

gaps.area: CrispCloud Office search fidelity and bounds
gaps.finding: Search follows relocated main/story parts, note references, workbook and slide order, used shared strings and speaker notes. Strict OOXML namespaces are recognized; external and escaping relationships are rejected; input and emitted UTF-8 text share bounded processing rules.

gaps.area: Actual host outputs and coverage provenance
gaps.finding: The host requires exactly forty-one valid captured DOCX outputs, then independently validates them with Open XML SDK. Fresh Office LCOV and engine VM reports list unhit instrumented lines, absent files and current source hashes. Helpers reject malformed records, missing source paths and out-of-range line numbers; clean-directory collection is required because same-length stale input cannot be detected from coverage alone.

gaps.area: Imported note marker position and absence
gaps.finding: Imported footnote and endnote markers are zero-width ordered inline tokens. Exact source position, kind, run properties and absence survive deep clone, minimal text edits and three save/reopen cycles, including nested table cells and marker-only notes. New-note layout uses the same superscript marker and separator as native export.
gaps.limits: The legacy whole-note text setter intentionally replaces rich content and preserves one automatic reference marker. Use paragraph/run operations for rich edits.

gaps.area: Rich run editing and native inline fields
gaps.finding: Coalescing, cloning, deletion, links and citations retain sparse styles, note tokens and native inline field metadata. Native citations no longer replace surrounding paragraph content. Field dispatch matches instruction commands, not words within quoted arguments.

gaps.area: TOC cached content and source formatting
gaps.finding: Page-number suppression, including native partial ranges, survives repeated exports without stripping trailing heading numerals. Export does not mutate live paragraph tabs.

gaps.area: Rich table merge and structural undo
gaps.finding: Merge retains ordered paragraphs, pictures, frames, nested tables and drawings; row/cell snapshots retain properties without aliasing. Editor history reuses live identities so later commands remain attached after replay.

gaps.area: Picture accessibility metadata and leading column breaks
gaps.finding: Native picture title and description remain independent of display name. A middle column break does not suppress an explicit leading column break.

Paragraph and margin dialogs retain fractional values, imported tab alignment and leaders, explicit zero and unedited properties. No-op Apply remains clean; selected and auxiliary-story edits are covered through real host controls.

gaps.area: Structural scripts and independent edit goldens
gaps.finding: Authored XML, three committed scripts and semantic JSON expectations cover create/edit/remove transitions across three save/reopen cycles. Invalid structures and late step failures preserve existing output.

Tracked revisions bind to the actual paragraph across body, header/footer, note and comment stories; imports, serialization and accept/reject no longer redirect to unrelated body indexes. Native export splits coalesced runs at exact revision boundaries and retains valid hyperlink/inline-field nesting.
gaps.limits: Imported note revisions resolve safely. Notes-pane whole-text replacement, structural/formatting changes and overlapping tracked ranges do not yet have complete native change-tracking semantics.

gaps.finding: Bibliography discovery follows internal customXml relationships and verifies namespaces. Export allocates collision-free owned parts and preserves unrelated custom XML. Rich imported sources retain structured authors, source types, GUIDs, publishers and extensions through scalar edits and source removal.
gaps.limits: New free-text authors are native literal corporate-author containers. Full personal-name parsing, native citation-style rendering and automatic retargeting of citation fields after direct tag mutation are not implemented.

gaps.finding: Simple inline native fields retain instruction, lock and dirty flags and remain atomic during supported edits. Automatic refresh preserves complex-field caches containing control/bookmark boundaries; destructive whole-field replacement is guarded. Arbitrarily nested, multi-run complex-field refresh still needs a richer range model.

Editor disjoint insertion/deletion and whole-span paragraph split/join rebase pending revision ranges, including auxiliary stories. Resolving an earlier change shifts later ranges. History restores target identity, bounds and conflict state. Destructive resolution and direct/isolate export validate bounds and recorded text before mutation. Scripted replaceText rebases pending ranges at the exact edited span.
gaps.limits: Intersecting edits, splits through pending spans and overlapping changes are explicit conflicts. Undo the conflicting edit before resolving or exporting. Arbitrary external model edits are rejected on mismatch, not attributed automatically.

gaps.area: Imported sparse styles after catalog introduction
gaps.finding: Introducing a heading/TOC style catalog no longer applies new-document spacing defaults to unrelated imported paragraphs; explicit defaults and overrides still cascade.
Independent controls reject dangling comment references, broken TOC targets, explicit false cantSplit, incorrect image relationship type and missing native field boundaries.

Late invalid arguments no longer partially mutate run formats, images, cells, stories or sections. Native cached fields reject partial ranges; TOC bookmark targets are unique, empty REF caches are explicit and visibility updates clear partial omission.
Replacing laid-out pages or compact mode invalidates layout, recalculating viewport extent and geometry before painting.
Open XML SDK rejected numeric bidiVisual values. Generated edits now write native on/off values, with positive repeated exports and a numeric-value corruption control.

gaps.area: Positioned frame wrapping in Quds layout
gaps.finding: Following body paragraphs and TOCs reflow around anchored square frames and clear top-and-bottom frames. Variable-width layout preserves bidi shaping and exact logical character ownership through multiple frames, columns, page transitions and note reservation. Native none/square/topBottom values, coordinates, dimensions, fill and stroke are checked against three authored raw source packages and nine repeated native exports.
gaps.limits: The model chooses one available line interval. Earlier paragraphs are not retroactively reflowed around later anchors. Arbitrary picture contours, floating table exclusions and full Microsoft Word layout equivalence remain unverified. Direct XML regressions cover preservation of explicit native outline width, dash, cap and join. The external frame corpus covers omitted/default outlines against its authored source. Quds canvas still previews frame outlines as solid fixed-width strokes; native outline styling is not visually reproduced there.

gaps.finding: Table and TOC selectors traverse modeled body containers in depth-first order and mutate the actual owner. Table merge uses logical grid columns; cell edits and unmerge use physical row-cell indexes. Uniform merged-grid addressing remains open.

Replace-all prepares and validates every affected paragraph before any mutation, rejects stale plans and unsupported later matches, and deduplicates repeated matches in atomic cached fields. Controller history retains rich tokens, native boundary identities and pending revision attribution in one undoable command.

One contained-block layout path measures and places paragraphs, pictures, nested tables, frames, TOCs, equations and transparent content controls. Source paragraph ownership stays stable across continued rows. Parent cell fill no longer hides rich children, ancestor cell clips no longer hide absolute frame text, and TOC page overlays align inside the actual cell or frame text box.
gaps.limits: This closes the named omissions and ownership regressions. It does not certify arbitrary table layout against Microsoft Word or every nested topology.

gaps.area: Tall-row rich content and physical page bounds
gaps.finding: Tall table rows retain anchored frames and pictures on their owning physical page, preserve global TOC targets, and reserve frame footnotes. Oversized inline pictures are bounded by the physical page and nested cell padding without changing model dimensions or image bytes. Live and reopened cases cover nested cells, continued rows and footnote contexts.
gaps.limits: Inline pictures may be reduced for layout to fit a page; source geometry is preserved in export. An impossible padding-only content region is rejected explicitly.

gaps.area: Native textbox insets, outlines and anchor presentation
gaps.finding: Native textbox insets, omitted-default semantics, anchor-paragraph properties, bodyPr metadata and line properties survive import/export and clone. Native line omission, omitted width and explicit width/cap/dash/join survive; changing stroke color retains the original width. Explicit inset edits update only owned values, with matching VML fallbacks. Text layout and the selected-frame ruler use the same left/right content box. All three frame wrap sources match their first native export and subsequent cycles exactly in LibreOffice.
gaps.limits: Frame layout and source presentation preservation are bounded by FID-056; full native textbox overflow and anchor semantics remain unverified. Direct XML regressions cover preservation of explicit native outline width, dash, cap and join. The external frame corpus covers omitted/default outlines against its authored source. Quds canvas still previews frame outlines as solid fixed-width strokes; native outline styling is not visually reproduced there.

gaps.area: Native inline math and TOC cache presentation
gaps.finding: Inline math retains its native inline/display wrapper. Native TOC cache paragraphs preserve paragraph count, tab/leader and run presentation, plus exact bookmark/control boundary ownership. Reconstructed cache ranges include the current page text while retaining the live entry paragraph owner; titles and field-only source paragraphs keep their own owners. All targets are preflighted before explicit refresh, so a later guarded cache cannot mutate earlier TOCs, heading aliases or controller history.
gaps.limits: Explicit regeneration of native TOC caches containing ranges is guarded until those ranges can be remapped safely; arbitrary rich complex-field refresh remains FID-049.

gaps.area: Native settings part ownership and namespaces
gaps.finding: Only modeled tracking, protection and odd/even-story settings are merged. Unowned native settings and attributes, including protection metadata, retain their source representation; an absent settings part is not invented. Changed or created owned elements bind a fresh local Word namespace prefix so aliased/default Word namespaces and foreign w attributes remain distinct.

gaps.area: Note-pane text replacement across bookmark ranges
gaps.finding: A note-pane text replacement that would remove only one bookmark endpoint is rejected before text, pending note commits, selection, dirty state or history changes. A complete in-note range can be removed safely. Generated paragraph aliases do not duplicate native identities.
gaps.limits: Safe remapping of a partially removed cross-paragraph range is not implemented; rich paragraph/run edits remain the supported alternative. This guard applies to the note-pane edit path, not every whole-note API; the legacy editNote operation intentionally replaces rich content.

gaps.area: LibreOffice import of native block controls in comments
gaps.finding: The independently authored source with block controls in comments is rejected by the available LibreOffice importer before Quds modifies it. The original seven source/export packages remain mandatory for semantic and Open XML SDK checks. Only exact-path, exact-SHA256, zero-error SDK receipts can qualify these files as native_schema_only after the raw source reproduces the specific importer refusal. Such files receive no visual certification. A separately authored seven-file header/footer-control corpus remains subject to strict source and repeated-cycle rendering.
gaps.limits: A native renderer that supports this topology is still needed for its visual certification. If a newer LibreOffice renders the source, normal strict comparisons automatically apply.

gaps.area: Scripted text replacement and tracked revision attribution
gaps.finding: Scripted replaceText rebases pending revision ranges after the exact accepted text edit. A repeated-text regression independently checks the original tracked span moves from [5,8] to [8,11], retaining author and content through exports. Rejected structural edits leave text and revision metadata unchanged; intersecting edits retain explicit conflict state.
gaps.limits: Ambiguous intersecting edits continue to use the explicit conflict rules in FID-050.

gaps.area: Scripted table deletion and native range ownership
gaps.finding: Row, column and TOC deletion preflight typed bookmark endpoints against every removed paragraph, including source-only native TOC cache owners. Cross-boundary deletion fails before mutation; complete-range deletion remains legal and surviving endpoint identities stay unchanged.
gaps.limits: This closes bookmark endpoint ownership for the named deletions; full tracked-change semantics for arbitrary structural edits remain outside FID-047.

gaps.area: CrispCloud style and custom tab controls
gaps.finding: The existing host dialog preserves imported tab alignment and leaders but does not offer creation of custom alignment/leader settings. Character-style editing, custom style creation and table-style selection remain UI gaps even though engine/script APIs support those properties.

Imported separator, continuationSeparator and continuationNotice definitions retain native absence, owner paths, properties and namespace context through adjacent edits, cloned note blocks and three save/reopen cycles. New note parts keep conventional definitions. Quds preview suppresses the line when imported definitions are absent.
gaps.limits: The preview absence fix does not reproduce arbitrary custom separator text, width, styles or distinct continuation rules.

gaps.finding: RTL, columns/sections, continued notes and tall-table goldens check the original plus each of three successive reopened documents and emit cycles 1, 2 and 3; no duplicate-byte stand-ins or unverified final reopen. The three-page first/even/default story scenario likewise checks its original plus three actual save/reopen states.

gaps.area: Native converter refusal diagnostics and qualification
gaps.finding: A zero-exit conversion without a PDF retains both output streams and exit status. Only the exact known source-load refusal may qualify the seven original auxiliary-control documents, subject to exact inventory, semantic/XML checks and matching clean SDK path/hash receipts. Crashes, timeouts, generic missing PDFs and stale receipts remain failures. Schema receipts are uploaded before rendering.
gaps.limits: Qualified packages receive native_schema_only status and no visual certification; see FID-065.

gaps.area: Auxiliary fixture schema property order and retained parts
gaps.finding: The authored footer emits paragraph spacing before alignment. Across every Word XML part, including retained parts no longer actively referenced, the independent oracle rejects spacing after alignment. It also checks exact spacing values in the PAGE footer. Open XML SDK owns full schema validation for every package part.

gaps.area: New note IDs versus preserved native definitions
gaps.finding: The shared note insertion path reserves live normal-note IDs plus retained special-definition IDs in the owning native notes part before allocating a normal note. Footnote and endnote ID domains remain separate; relocated note parts are resolved through their owning relationship. Existing live-note numbering remains monotonic, and unrelated higher special IDs do not force unnecessary renumbering.
gaps.limits: This protects the shared insertion API used by the editor; arbitrary direct mutation of model IDs is not assigned a new identity automatically.

evidence_path_convention: Unprefixed paths are relative to quds_office_suite; CrispCloud: paths are relative to the host repository.
